description: a solo who likes the space
summary:
Sol 10: NASA Outpost Commander is an interactive 3D space-survival and mission-command game built in React, TypeScript, and Three.js for kids ages 7–12. Players take command of a lunar or Martian outpost, balancing limited power, oxygen, radiation shielding, and mission lifespan across a 10-day timeline.
To address the challenge of making real deep-space engineering intuitive for young learners, the game enforces a strict "no free lunch, no undo" rule: every choice permanently deducts mission days and triggers real-time 3D visual consequences—such as deploying water-wall radiation shields or firing rocket stabilizers in dust gales—alongside a clue-based AI helper (Bot-11). Cadets train on four real historical crises (Apollo 12, 2003 Halloween Solar Storm, Opportunity’s 2018 Dust Storm, and Perseverance Sol 313) before unlocking Live Mode, which pulls real-time solar flare telemetry from NASA’s DONKI API alongside OSDR and PDS science principles.
This bridges abstract space facts and authentic mission planning, empowering kids to think like real NASA flight directors.
details:
Sol 10: NASA Outpost Commander is a browser-based 3D space-survival and mission-command simulation designed for children ages 7–12. Players log in as a Space Cadet, select an avatar and lunar or Martian outpost, and start a 10-day mission managing power, oxygen, radiation shielding, and spacecraft stability.

Every turn presents a real space emergency with three decisions. Following a strict "no free lunch, no undo" rule, every choice permanently deducts 1 to 5 Mission Days and triggers immediate, real-time 3D consequences on the outpost—such as pumping water into habitat shield walls during solar flares, firing rocket stabilizer thrusters in high-wind dust gales, or entering battery hibernation when dust blocks sunlight. Cadets first complete a 4-mission Historical Training Academy to earn 300 Science Points, unlocking Live NASA DONKI Mode, where today’s actual solar flare telemetry shapes the mission in real time.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Turns Abstract Science into Systems Thinking: Instead of memorizing space facts, young players experience why saving power today can cause freezing batteries or oxygen shortages tomorrow.
  • Active Critical Thinking (Bot-11 Clue System): Rather than giving away answers, spending a mission day to consult robotic co-pilot Bot-11 reveals a real NASA physics clue, encouraging kids to reason through thermal mass, air filtration, and radiation shielding on their own.
  • Accessible STEM Inspiration: Zero downloads, zero passwords, plain-language prompts, and a personalized printable Junior NASA Flight Director Certificate make it immediately usable in classrooms, libraries, and homes.

Creativity & Design Inspiration

  • Cinematic Storytelling: Inspired by The Martian’s "science-the-problem" engineering mindset and Interstellar’s compounding time-cost tension and witty robotic co-pilot banter.
  • Living 3D Space Environment: Instead of static text cards or disconnected video popups, players command an interactive 3D lunar/Martian outpost set beneath a live solar system with orbiting relay satellites, Deep Space Network (DSN) telemetry beams, and an autonomous scanning rover.
  • Training-to-Live Progression: Grounding players in famous historical NASA emergencies before letting them command today's live space weather builds confidence and replayability.

Tools, Coding Languages & NASA Open Data Used

  • Languages & Frameworks: TypeScript (100%), React, Vite, Tailwind CSS
  • 3D Graphics & Animation: Three.js (@react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei), Framer Motion
    • NASA DONKI API (FLR): Real-time and historical solar flare telemetry driving live space-weather alerts.
    • NASA OSDR: Spaceflight radiation dosimetry and thermal biology principles informing crew shielding mechanics.
    • NASA PDS & Perseverance MEDA: Martian dust storm solar-power drops (Opportunity 2018) and Sol 313 high-wind dust gale dynamics.
    • Apollo 12 Flight Journal: 1969 electrostatic sensor glitch and auxiliary backup circuit (SCE to Aux) recovery logic.

Key Factors Considered

  • Cognitive Load for Ages 7–12: Consolidated complex spacecraft engineering into three clear visual meters (Mission Lifespan, Suit Air & Shielding, and Lander Power & Stability) with concise choice cards under 15 words.
  • API Reliability & Offline Resilience: Implemented 1-hour localStorage caching, .env API key protection, offline historical fallbacks, and a "Test Solar Storm Alert" toggle so demos work reliably even during quiet solar days or low-connectivity conditions
